...Hehe. You trusted me, didn't you?
There's no need to worry. You'll be feeling all better soon.

Just as you say, it seems this cat made this park its home...
As far as I know, it's always here all alone.

I wanted to take it to the vet if I could. But whenever I try to get close,
it retreats further back. I really want to help it, though...

Until then... I'll stay by your side so you don't feel lonely.
So that you can meet someone kind... and find happiness.

That's why—hang in there.
We've finally made it this far, after all.

Probably. It seems to be bothered by its tummy sometimes... See, there it goes again.
...Its gaze and its voice both seem to carry a hint of pain and discomfort.

...I see you're still not in the mood for that yet.
Hehe. Whenever you feel like it is fine, I'll be right here.
Meoow~♪

Little kitty. After the clinic, shall we look for a new home together?
I'll reach out to all kinds of people to see if anyone can adopt you.
The girl's smile was pure enough to make anyone who saw it believe so.

—My name is Victoire Pisa.
I attend Tracen Academy. It is a pleasure to meet you.

So, if it's all right with you... would you let a vet take a look at you?
There's nothing to be scared of. I'll stay right by your side the whole time.
Illuminated by the glow of the streetlamp, the girl smiles.

Hehe, looks like you find it quite cozy.
It'll take a little longer to get to the clinic, but we can rest easy for now.

Hehe.
I wonder if you understand what I'm saying.

This little one... must be terrified of people.
And since it seems to be sick or injured, all the more so.

Yes. I wanted to stay by its side to reassure it.
To let it know, "You are not alone"...

She had an airy, gentle aura about her.
I wondered who she was talking to. Following her gaze—

—That day.
I truly believe I met an angel.

Actually, I brought some too.
However, it won't eat unless it lets its guard down...

...?
Ah... yes, that's right.

Is "pure and innocent" the right phrase? I felt her actions were rooted
in something fundamentally different from the ordinary urge to rescue a cute animal.
Little kitty, I promise I'll find you wonderful foster parents.

...This kitty definitely needs treatment. That's why—
I just want to stay until it understands, "You don't need to be afraid."
...Meoow.

At a park I visited during my early morning walk.
An Umamusume was crouching before a bush, talking to something.

Once you're able to eat properly again,
I'll give you some delicious canned cat food to celebrate.

Ah—heheh♪
You're right.

Ah—the person from this morning...
Thank you for your concern.

—She was there.
Out in the pouring rain. In the exact same spot as this morning.

No, no, please don't worry about it.
I was merely talking to the cat on my own, anyway.

At last, the cat approached her outstretched hand, timidly at first—
until it began rubbing its forehead against her.

Yes. Thank you for your kindness.
Let's stay together until the kitty comes out.

Look, see?
It came much closer than it did this morning.

Crouching beside her to peek in, the cat glared at me
and backed away into the depths of the bushes. It wouldn't give me the time of day.
"Let's stay together until the kitty comes out."

In the rain showing no sign of stopping, I kept her company in her quiet bonding with the cat.
And then—

...
...Come here.

It's getting chilly, isn't it...? It would be terrible if you caught a cold.
I have some towels here, so you can bundle up in them just like a blanket.

As if the clear morning skies were a lie,
raindrops began to fall from the heavy, overcast clouds.

It's all right... You're safe now. There's nothing to be afraid of.
Would you please come over here, just for a moment? Come on—
After parting ways with her, as I was wrapping up my errands—
—Perhaps this is what an angel's smile looks like.

Afterward, I found an emergency veterinary clinic open late and went along with her.
It seemed she had already prepared everything necessary to transport the cat.

On the hill now swallowed by darkness, only the quiet pitter-patter of rain could be heard.
Assuming she had surely gone home by now—

—In the evening, on my way back from running errands.
Amidst the pouring rain, thoughts of the Umamusume and the cat from this morning crossed my mind once again.
